NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to apply a controlled micro-texture to the comb finger surfaces to create nano-scale air pockets that reduce contact area during shock events. Standard practice applies a hydrophobic coating to prevent stiction, but this intervention creates a mechanical barrier through surface texturing that reduces van der Waals forces and capillary action regardless of contamination. The closest existing technique is laser surface texturing for wear reduction in mechanical bearings, but our approach differs by targeting the specific scale of MEMS comb fingers (micrometers) to create air pockets that maintain separation under shock loads without adding bulk.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the adhesion force F_adh = (γ·A)/d, where γ is the surface energy, A is the contact area, and d is the separation distance. By creating a micro-texture with feature sizes of 1-5 μm and depths of 0.5-1 μm, we reduce the effective contact area A by >90% while maintaining the nominal gap between fingers. This reduces adhesion forces by an order of magnitude, making them insufficient to overcome the restoring force of the suspension springs even under 10,000 g shock.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
Standard practice: (a) Hydrophobic coating process (already present)
Intervention:
(b) Micro-texture stamping tool (procurable standard MEMS fabrication tool)
(c) Surface texturing process parameter change (reducing etch time by 30% to create controlled micro-roughness)
(b) Post-texture cleaning solution (procurable standard MEMS cleaning fluid)
(c) Inspection protocol change (using existing optical inspection equipment with modified criteria)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —
Standard practice uses 1 coating process + 1 design parameter.
Intervention replaces coating process with texturing process (same burden class), adds no additional equipment (stamp tool is standard MEMS equipment), and modifies existing inspection protocol (no new hardware). Burden is same class as standard practice.

EXECUTABLE TEST —
Protocol: Subject 50 devices to 10,000 g shock in X, Y, and Z axes (10 shocks per axis, 30 total per device). Measure zero-g offset before and after shock using calibrated reference accelerometer. Pass/fail criterion: permanent zero-g offset ≤50 mg. Duration: 1 week for testing. Kill criterion: any device showing >50 mg permanent offset after shock testing fails. Control group: 50 identical devices with standard coating subjected to identical shock testing.

FEASIBILITY AUDIT (V5):
Micro-texture stamping tool - (b) - procurable standard MEMS fabrication tool
Surface texturing process parameter change - (c) - modification to existing etching equipment
Post-texture cleaning solution - (b) - procurable standard MEMS cleaning fluid
Inspection protocol change - (c) - modification to existing optical inspection equipment
